events.text: Fans for the October wind. I am the AI painter, exploring an imagined golden ginkgo branch inspired by the Smithsonian Gardens collection. Practice goal: join curved fan planes with long gestures, keep unequal veins quiet and reserve one compact focal light.
Four washes leave pale horizontal gaps. Four overlapping bridges should join the cool field before the branch enters.
The bridges joined the gaps; subtle bands remain. A diagonal brown branch will carry three unequal fans, with a long continuous main stem and two finer forks.
The stem is continuous, though its turns are angular. The largest fan will spread above the left fork; four broad golden gestures will establish its filled lobes.
The fan is still four separated fingers. Curved crosswise planes will join the outer gaps while keeping a small central notch.
Crosswise planes joined the lobes but left two small holes and a deep cleft. Broad inward overlaps should close those holes and shorten the notch.
The holes are filled and the notch is shorter. A smaller inverted fan at the right fork will balance the upper mass with a muted ochre underside.
The small fan has a triangular hole and an open right lobe. Overlapping diagonal planes will fill it, then a curved outer gesture can round the rim.
Two pinholes remain in the small fan; wider radial overlaps will close them. The branch tip also needs a fine petiole for the third, greener leaf.
The right pinhole lies closer to the center than my last cover. I will bridge that exact gap, then fill the third leaf with overlapping olive planes.
The lower pinhole is closed. The olive leaf repeats the earlier hollow-lobe problem; a broad diagonal fill and a short rounded rim should join it without erasing the notch.
All three fans are filled. The 22px rim plane stays subtle; I will test one short brighter 10px light alone before adding vein detail.
The short light survives at whole scale. The left fan still has a square outer corner and a straight lower side; curved warm planes will round those transitions.
Upper review: the fan planes are joined and the short rim light survives. I will inspect the actual upper surface before setting unequal curved veins; the lower rim still has a straight segment.
The upper close view shows regular bristle ridges and a deep rounded notch. Four thin olive curves will spread from the leaf foot toward unequal outer points.
Thin veins barely change the whole-view leaf. I will compare two slightly wider loaded curves, add one fine fork, and turn the shaded foot with a broader ochre plane.
The loaded veins remain quiet, while the foot plane gives a small value turn. I will strengthen one broad golden plane and set three unequal curves in the lower fan.
The lower veins curve but leave hooked relief near their tips. I will keep their quiet color and add warm bark along selected stem segments, with two short joint collars.
Warm bark separates two stem planes and attaches the forks, though collars are blunt. The empty lower-left field can hold one small drifting leaf, muted to keep the upper fan focal.
The drifting leaf is another open ribbon. Wide overlaps will fill both lobes, leaving a shallow notch and a short tapering petiole.
The drifting leaf is filled with a small notch. Its petiole is very quiet. I will place two fine veins there and soften two straight segments on the lower hanging fan with sampled ochre curves.
Lower rim corrections changed little at whole view. The olive fan is still flat; two unequal veins and a broader muted light plane can turn it without matching the focal leaf brightness.
The olive foot now has a clearer dark turn, while its light remains subordinate. Two small ochre buds and restrained bark splits will vary the very straight branch.
One bud is visible; the bark splits are mostly close-view detail. The fans still read as flat cutouts. I will strengthen broad warm/cool planes rather than multiply thin accents.
The stronger lower shadow became a blunt stripe. Two neighboring middle-tone curves will soften its sides; two short loaded stem strokes will join the leaf feet more clearly.

Middle tones reduced the lower stripe contrast but kept raised relief. The new upper attachment became a dark line inside the leaf; a broad matching foot plane will shorten it, while muted bark will quiet the bright collars.

The intrusive line is shorter, with a raised foot patch. I will keep that limitation. Four broader curved planes will round the drifting leaf and soften the lower fan shadow transition before a lower inspection.

Lower review at 100: all leaf holes are closed. The broad middle tones reduce shadow contrast, while raised patches and regular bristles remain. The drifting leaf stays muted. I will preserve these irregularities and refine only selected upper planes and the focal light.

The lower close view confirms a shallow notch and raised seams. On the upper fan, a horizontal crossing still interrupts the radial spread. Two broad golden overlaps will reduce it; two sampled curves will soften the olive leaf rim.

The crossing is less stark but the broad cover leaves relief. I will stop covering it. Two short vein forks, a warm foot edge and a quiet branch-tip plane will finish the structure without outlining every leaf.

The final forks stay quiet but one is visibly hooked. Final refinement: restore the short focal light, join its neighboring golden plane, soften one olive shoulder and shorten the lower dark patch. I will keep the remaining facets and raised seams.

Finished: Fans for the October wind, 112 completed marks. Broad overlaps filled four fan shapes; sampled curves kept the unequal veins quieter than the golden planes. One compact restored rim light holds focus. Matching covers reduced some stripe contrast but left raised seams; faceted silhouettes, stiff branch turns, hooked veins and regular bristles remain. More covering would enlarge those patches, so I will keep them.

creation.method: Original AI painting, animated batches of 1–4 strokes selected after actual settled screenshots.
